title: A dip on a blade cut inside one clip can hold on black too
goal: Holding on black between the fade down and the fade up only works where two separate clips meet. A cut made with the blade inside one recording shows no Hold on black row, so the common case of cutting a screen recording and dipping to black cannot sit on black for a beat.
notes: Found while building a-transition-can-sit-before-across-or-after-the (2026-09-28). The hold is ClipTransition.holdMS; between clips it is the gap between the two clips (editPoints accepts gap == arrival hold, editPointCut reads the gap as the hold, PhotonzDocument.setTransition ripples). Inside one clip the pieces butt, so ClipPieces.setTransition refuses holdMS > 0 and EditorState.canHoldClipTransition is false for .join. Doing it there means pieces carrying a hold gap in startMS/totalLengthMS, or splitting the clip at the join into two clips when a hold is asked for.
acceptance: A dip on a join inside one clip shows the Hold on black row
Choosing a hold inserts that much black inside the clip, moves everything after it along, and one undo takes it back out
A walk at Next defaults sets a hold on a blade cut and claims what moved

log.note: Before building: in Premiere a blade leaves two clips and a black hold is the gap between them, so a hold on a join cuts the clip in two at the join and reuses the between-clips hold (ripple, black panel, silent sound, timeline Black block) rather than teaching every piece-timing reader about a gap inside one clip (about 30 files read piece offsets). Visible cost: one clip becomes two. That goes in the audit's evaluate for the user to judge.
